papers.title: An Adaptive Strategy for Active Learning with Smooth Decision Boundary
papers.abstract: We present the first adaptive strategy for active learning in the setting of classification with smooth decision boundary. The problem of adaptivity (to unknown distributional parameters) has remained opened since the seminal work of Castro and Nowak (2007), which first established (active learning) rates for this setting. While some recent advances on this problem establish adaptive rates in the case of univariate data, adaptivity in the more practical setting of multivariate data has so far remained elusive. Combining insights from various recent works, we show that, for the multivariate case, a careful reduction to univariate-adaptive strategies yield near-optimal rates without prior knowledge of distributional parameters.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及主动学习策略，但与有限元代理建模、不确定性量化或生物力学设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is purely about active learning for classification theory and provides no cover of FEA surrogate modeling, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification, or biomechanics transferability.

summary_zh.method: 将多元问题简化为单变量自适应策略以获得近最优速率。

summary_en.motivation: To achieve adaptivity in active learning for multivariate classification with smooth decision boundaries.
summary_en.method: A reduction to univariate adaptive strategies yields near-optimal rates for the multivariate setting.
summary_en.result: Near-optimal rates are obtained without prior knowledge of distributional parameters.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical analysis with no experimental validation.
